newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares jump 3.6 percent on easier credit.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares jump 3.6 percent on easier credit.

text.p: Delhi shares closed with widespread gains, surging 3.6 percent as last weekend's credit easing by the central bank continued to stoke buying, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's benchmark index ended up 26.07 points at 751.75.
Sunil Prabhaker of Spurt Securities said the weekend moves by the Reserve Bank of India to ease credit raised expectations that more funds would be invested in the stock markets.
A general rise in the prices of global depositary receipts (GDRs) in overseas markets underpinned the rally, Prabhaker said.
Cement maker ACC added 97 rupees to 1,648.
Reliance Industries jumped 8.75 rupees to 215.45 on buying by domestic financial institutions.
TISCO gained 16.50 rupees to 191.60 on scattered buying by investors.
State Bank of India rose 12.90 rupees to 241.50 in active trade.
Financial houses snapped up shares in Hindustan Lever, which rose 14 rupees to 824.
Two-wheeler maker Bajaj Auto added 10 rupees to 985 on scattered buying support.
TELCO rose 10 rupees to 441 on brisk buying by investors.
